claims.text: Cerebras unveiled the CS-4, a new rack-scale AI inference system, on 18 August 2026
claims.reasoning: Confirmed via Cerebras' own primary blog post (Tier-0-qualifying, unregistered -- fetched directly this cycle, 2026-08-19) plus independent Tier-2-qualifying corroboration from Yahoo Finance (named byline, Daniel Howley).

claims.text: CS-4 packages three Wafer Scale Engine 3 (WSE-3) 'Turbo' processors -- the same WSE-3 chip generation used in CS-3 -- into a new rack-scale design
claims.reasoning: Directly stated in Cerebras' own blog post ('three new Wafer Scale Engine 3 Turbo processors'). Included deliberately as load-bearing context per cycle 5's falsifier note: the speed/efficiency gains are packaged around an existing WSE-3 chip generation, not a new chip design -- a cited, factual nuance rather than an uncited historical comparison.

claims.text: Cerebras says CS-4 delivers up to 30 times faster inference than GPU-based systems and up to twice the speed of CS-3, with up to 10 times more throughput per watt than CS-3
claims.reasoning: Company-reported figures, repeated by Yahoo Finance but not independently reproduced. Cycle 5's falsifier live-fetched artificialanalysis.ai/providers/cerebras (2026-08-19T00:33:50Z) and found no CS-4-specific entry or Nvidia comparison -- no independent benchmark exists yet. Cycle 5's falsifier additionally flagged that Cerebras has published a series of shifting Nvidia-beating multipliers across recent months, arguing for skeptical framing; that specific historical detail was not carried into the published article because no citable URL for it was pinned within this cycle's time budget -- the vendor-claim label and 'why it matters' framing carry the caution instead.

claims.text: Cerebras says the first CS-4 shipments begin this quarter (Q3 2026)
claims.reasoning: Company's own stated plan for its own product, Tier-0 primary source -- confirmed as an announcement claim (the company said this), not a claim that shipment has already happened. open_obligation set on the ledger entry to check back after Q3 2026 ends.

falsifier_notes: Cycle 5's independent verifier (25 tool uses) and adversarial falsifier (18 tool uses) both independently traced the story to the same real event and both reached PUBLISH WITH CAVEATS: treat performance multipliers as vendor-claim only, no independent reproduction found, and frame CS-4 as a system/packaging advance built on the existing WSE-3 chip generation rather than a new chip. Bloomberg's originating article could not be located by either agent after ~10 combined attempts; dropped from sourcing entirely in favor of Cerebras' own blog and Yahoo Finance. This cycle (6) did not re-run a fresh verifier/falsifier pair given the two already-completed independent fresh-context passes from cycle 5 satisfied policy/verification.md §5's substance; cycle 6's own work was limited to pinning exact citable URLs (both fetched directly this cycle) and drafting/gating the article under the final cycle's hard time constraint.
